The survey, conducted August 7-10 among 1,913 registered voters, found that 55 percent disapprove of Trump's performance as president. It also found that Trump's net approval rating among Republicans, a measure of the gap between approval and disapproval, fell 8 percentage points from the previous month.

More than half of registered voters said they are worse off financially since Trump's return to office. [...] The Financial Times/Focaldata poll found similar concerns. Among registered voters, 64 percent disapproved of Trump's handling of inflation and the cost of living, including nearly seven in 10 independents and about one-third of Republicans.

Noble Predictive Insights released a poll showing that the president has a net approval rating of -19 among Arizona registered voters, meaning 39% approve of Trump’s job performance while 58% disapprove.

Trump’s approval rating has declined by 6 points since May, when his net approval rating was -13. [...] The Republicans with the highest favorability ratings are  U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio; U.S. Rep. Andy Biggs, R-Gilbert, and Vice President JD Vance.

Rubio’s net favorability rating is at 2%, while Biggs is at 0%. Vance’s net favorability rating came in at -5%.

Trump’s net favorability rating is -13%.

Trump’s job approval in August stands at 40%, while disapproval is at 59%. This is the same approval level as in July, while disapproval has increased one percentage point, from 58%. This ties the record low of approval in either Trump’s first or second terms, and is a new record low for his net approval, at -19 percentage points.
